rationale: Bus protocols expose channels, not memory-mapped registers

extraction_strategy.ic_class_applicability_gate_v0_1_62: ic_class='bus_interconnect_protocol' declares LL4 not applicable; emitted as N/A stub (l_doc_taxonomy.na_stub)

notes: If a future system-integration L4 is required, the canonical 'address-side fields' to capture would be: address-map regions per slave, per-region TileLink conformance level, per-region cacheability / FIFO / executeability / privilege / QoS, source ID width (o bits per master interface), sink ID width (i bits per slave interface), address width (a bits per link), and data bus width (w bytes per link). The TileLink protocol spec itself carries no architectural register map; implementation-side configuration registers (if any) are exposed through the second TileLink agent inside an interconnect module rather than via this layer.
base_address: Defined at SoC level; offsets given relative to module base.

address_side_field_widths.a_o_source_id_width: o bits (per-link, unique per master interface)
address_side_field_widths.d_i_sink_id_width: i bits (per-link, unique per slave interface)

address_space_properties: FIFO ordering requirements (optional FIFO domain identifier)
